title: Get motivated and stay motivated
seo_title: Get motivated and stay motivated - Team One Fitness
seo_description: Want to get fit and healthy? Check out some things you can do to get motivated and increase your success rate of getting and staying into a healthy routine.
content:
Spring has definitely started, daylight savings is about to start and after having the winter blues, many people want to get motivated, fit and healthy for summer. Getting out of your winter blues and back into a training routine is often easier said than done. Here a few things you can do to get motivated and increase your success rate of getting and staying in a healthy routine.

Have a plan

Make an exercise plan make the necessary bookings or arrangements because this will help you to stick to your plan. Booking in for a session means that you've made a commitment ahead of the session and you’ll be less likely to change your plan or come up with excuses not to go.

Try group training

Group training with like-minded people with the same or similar training goals works as a great motivator. Knowing that it is not just you who is struggling to get through a workout routine can help you push yourself to your limits. Having other people around you might make the difference between quitting when you’re tired and pushing yourself a bit more!

Challenge yourself

To stay motivated it is important to keep giving yourself challenges. These challenges or goals can be big or small. It’s a good idea to start with the bigger challenges and then to break these down into smaller once. Think about what you need to do reach your bigger goals. For example, to be able to run 15km’s without stopping in 3 months, you might need to do 2 running sessions per week and run 5km in the first week.

Work out with a buddy

Training with a buddy can be very motivating. If you’ve made arrangements with your workout buddy to go to a class then the last thing you want to do is let them down. A workout buddy with a similar fitness level can push you so you reach your goals quicker.

Eat the right nutrition

Eating the right nutrition is important when you want to lead an active lifestyle. Give your body the nutrition it needs to function properly. Remember, often nutrition and exercise go hand in hand. Having a healthy diet can motivate you to start exercising and on the other hand doing an Amazing workout can motivate you to have a clean balanced diet.

Be proud of yourself and enjoy!

Get motivated and be proud of it. Be proud of yourself for being motivated and active. Embrace change and enjoy the amazing benefits of exercising. Enjoy the endorphins after a great workout and the progress that you’re making. A new season is a great time to start a new routine and these easy, motivating ideas will help you get started. Soon, you’ll become a healthier and happier you for the new season ahead.

title: How water can improve weight loss
seo_description: Are you getting enough water and did you know that water can improve weight loss? Here are some surprising facts about how water can help with weight loss.
content:
Most people know how important it is to drink enough water. Here is an article that shows some surprising facts about how water can improve weight loss. The easiest trick that can help you with losing fat faster is drinking more water.

Check out the following facts:

  • 80% of Australians suffer from symptoms typical of dehydration and the majority don't recognise key symptoms.
  • Even MILD dehydration will slow down your metabolism by 3%.
  • One glass of water will shut down midnight hunger pains for most people.
  • Lack of water is the #1 trigger for day time fatigue.
  • Drinking 5 glasses of water daily decreases the risk of colon cancer by 45%, breast cancer by 79%, and bladder cancer by 50%.
  • A low water intake interferes with efficient fat metabolism.
  • Water can be use as a natural laxative helping to relieve constipation.
  • You could loss up to 4.5kg of fat in 1 year by just increasing you water intake.

Other anti-aging benefits include:

  • better skin hydration to reduce wrinkles
  • a reduction in back and joint pain
  • increased energy
  • disease prevention

So how much water should you drink?

A lot of people believe that 2 litres is the recommended daily amount for everyone but the amount needed varies and depends on individual factors such as age, diet, climate and levels of physical activity. For men aged between 19 and 70 years of age, it is actually considered to be around 2.6 litres or about 8 to 10 glasses of water. If you need to up your water intake, try and increase your water intake by about 20% a week until your intake is sufficient. You'll find yourself more alert with more energy and you may just surprise yourself with busting through a fat loss plateau.

Some other tips on how to keep hydrated

  • Train yourself to drink more water by linking drinking water to other activities such as waking up, doing the dishes, training, starting to work on your desk, etc.
  • Drink two glasses of water when you wake up and another glass when you arrive at work.
  • Fill a reusable bottle with water at your work. This will make it easier to measure how much water you're taking in.

title: Some tips when fast food is unavoidable
seo_description: Life is fast and we all experience situations where 'fast food' is the only choice. Here are some tips when fast food is unavoidable.
content:
Life is fast and we all experience situations where 'fast food' is the only choice when you are in a hurry or in certain locations, here are some tips when fast food is unavoidable. Although fast food places are starting to offer more healthy options these days, keep in mind that in general they don't have your health in mind. If you're in a situation where you MUST eat at a fast food restaurant, here are a few tips to keep in mind so you don't undo all the progress you are making at bootcamp!  

Keep the calories down

  • If you're ordering a burger which is roughly 800 calories, then there is no need to go the full monty and order fries and a sugary soda ... even if they're tempting you to upgrade to a meal deal for minimal additional cost!
  • If you order a burger, you could only eat one side of the bun. This will reduce your carb intake and keep the calories down. These types of carbs are not very nutritional anyway.
  • Go for small rather than extra large. Keep your meal small which will fill you up until you can have a proper meal. 
 

Avoid the liquid calories

Again, even if you are ordering a 'meal', try and avoid all the liquid calories and order a bottle of water instead. Sugary drinks don't fill you up and these empty calories will just promote your fat storage.  

Protein overboard

  • We all know that protein is great and a good source of energy but don't eat the whole cow! Keep the portions small but just enough to give you enough energy until you can have a healthier meal.
  • Also remember that the protein sources from fast food restaurants tend to be deep fried and so are laden with saturated fat.
  • Try and avoid burgers and opt for grilled chicken if this is available.
 

Be aware of toppings

Be aware of topping burgers with cheese, bacon, sauces etc. This will only add more saturated fat to your meal and bump up the calories.   Last but not least, always aim to have some healthy snacks with you. Carry some apples, nuts or even a low carb protein bar when you're on the go.  Some fast food restaurants sell fruit and healthier snacks. Life is about balance and it isn't easy to keep a clean diet all the time. If you get trapped and have an unhealthy fast food meal, make up for it with a fat burning activity or come and join one of our Sydney's Eastern Suburbs bootcamp sessions.

title: Get fit for summer fast
seo_description: Do you want to get fit for summer fast but are not sure where to start? Here a few tips which will give you that summer body in the fastest possible way.
content:
With temperatures rising, I am sure that a lot of people want to get fit for summer.  Ideally you have been keeping fit during winter which will make this process a lot easier. Others suddenly realise that there is a bit of work to be done and are not sure where to start. Here a few tips on how to get fit for summer in the fastest possible way.

High Intensity Intervals

If you want to get fit fast, high intensity interval training is the way to go. These workouts produce a big calorie burn in a short amount of time and are most effective. Interval training sessions are in general fairly short, but you need to put in the right amount of effort to keep the intensity high. If you do HIIT, it is a good idea to combine cardio exercises such as star jumps with full body resistance exercises such as thrusters or squats. Not sure where to start? Do Tabata workout sets which includes 8 rounds of 20 second bursts of an exercise with a 10 second rest in between.

Move More

Remember "small changes can make a difference", no matter if your goal is to increase your daily calorie expenditure, build muscle or get fit. Be creative and think about things that you can do to make this happen and reach your goals faster. Do some planks or glutes bridges while you watch TV, do some calf raises while brushing your teeth or washing the dishes. Do you spend tim every day on public transport? Maybe consider jumping on your bike and riding to work. Are you having an active lunch break? If not, go for a walk, run or join our Domain bootcamp session. There are plenty of things you can do but it all comes down to making your life more active.

Diet is more important than you think

If your goal is to lose weight then it is important to realise that diet will play a bigger role than exercise. Eat healthy wholesome food. Load up on veggies, eat lean protein and incorporate healthy fats in your meals. Not too sure where to start and want some more tips? Check out this link which has some general guidelines which might help.

Lift Weights

Incorporate strength training into your workouts. Short workouts with challenging weights will throw your metabolism into high gear and build lean muscle fast. This is why strength training is a must if you want to get fit fast. I recommend compound exercises such as overhead shoulder presses, pull ups, squats, squat upright rows, etc. Always remembers that the more muscles involved, the higher your overall calorie burn will be. If you want to focus on a specific part of your body such as the back of your arms, you can always do more isolated exercises for those specific muscles and for example do dips, triceps extension, etc.

Use Your Body

No access to equipment, no worries! Your own bodyweight gives you plenty of options to train yourself. If you want some ideas for body weight workouts, check out the following link.

Train with a trainer

Working with a personal trainer is one of the fastest and most effective ways to improve your health and fitness, and achieve your personal goals. A trainer provides structure and accountability, and helps you to develop a lifestyle that encourages positive health and nutrition practices. For more information about our Eastern Suburbs bootcamp sessions, please click here. If you want to get results faster and work with me one-on-one, check out Team One Fitness' personal training services and get in touch.

Combine Strength and Cardio

Combining strength with cardio while working out can be very effective. Think about a circuit where you perform a strength exercises such as squats (e.g. 25 reps), followed by a short 30 seconds intense exercise such as burpees or Squat thrusts. Training this way is effective because you're engaging large muscle groups to build strength while also increasing your heart rate to maximize calorie burn. When you add the cardio component using the same muscle group (e.g. squat jumps), you build endurance and burn more calories. On the other hand, short bursts of cardio will activate EPOC (excess post exercise oxygen consumption) which helps you burn more calories even after you've finished working out.

Sleep More

Not enough sleep can be detrimental to your health and hinder your weight loss goals. Lack of sleep will make you less likely to workout but it will also affect your appetite, a factor that very few people with weight loss goals fail to consider.  Sleep helps to regulate your appetite, metabolism and energy expenditure. When you sleep too little your body produces ghrelin, a hormone secreted by the stomach that tells the brain that we want to keep eating, and less leptin, a hormone that tells the brain that we're full and satisfied.

Avoid Carbs at Night

Try to avoid carbs at night, especially processed carbs such as white bread, white rice and added sugars. Aim to make your breakfast bigger than your lunch and lunch bigger than dinner. Avoid complex carbs after dinner. Complex carbohydrates are great for energy, but they need to eaten at the right time and during the day. If you're still hungry after dinner, choose for a healthy snack such as a handful of almonds. Your metabolism starts to naturally slow down towards the end of the day, which makes it more likely that those recently digested carbs will be stored as unnecessary fat. Also, your insulin sensitivity is believed to be reduced at night, which may also lead to fat storage.

title: Nutritional guidelines
seo_description: Here are a few nutritional tips that will improve your diet. Combine a healthy diet with an active lifestyle and burn more calories then you are taking in.
content:
Here are a few nutritional tips that will help you to improve and get a healthy balanced diet. There are many different diets around and some of them are more hardcore then others. All the various types of diets and opinions can be confusing. ?The following tips are less drastic but they refer to basic nutritional guidelines to get yourself back on track. It's a good way to start and by following these simple tips you should be able to get some results, shed some weight and feel better. Remember, combine a healthy diet with an active lifestyle. From the moment you are burning more calories then you are taking in, you start to lose weight. I know it is easier said than done but it's the truth.? Please let me know if you have any questions.
  • Reduce the consumption of carbohydrates and increase your intake of protein. Eat protein with every meal and choose protein from different sources, e.g. fish, eggs, meat, poultry, lentils, etc.
  • Increase the consumption of 'good' fats and reduce the consumption of 'bad' fats.
  • Reduce your alcohol consumption and be extremely conscious of the foods consumed while you drink; i.e. burgers and chips .
  • Decrease your amount of carbohydrates consumed as the day progresses and activity levels decrease. Rather have your carbs in the morning and at lunchtime and depending on your weight loss goals, maybe have none for dinner.
  • Eat breakfast, lunch and dinner with snacks in between. Increase your metabolism by having 5/6 meals a day. Make breakfast your most important meal of the day and don't skip meals.
  • Drink 8 glasses water each day or 2 litres. Have a glass of water before your meal. This helps fill you up before you eat.
  • Choose clean, natural and non-processed foods.

Last but not least a few general tips:

  • Be organised, make your meal plan and make sure you have all the ingredients at home.
  • Choose a meal plan which is easy to maintain.
  • Control what's in your food by cooking yourself.
  • Remember everything in moderation.
  • Include variety in your diet.

title: Benefits of beach training
seo_description: Most of Team One Fitness bootcamp sessions are on the beach. Not sure about the whole beach exercising thing? Check out some benefits of beach training.
content:
I absolutely love working out on the beach! Coming down to our early morning Bondi or Coogee bootcamp sessions is a very inspiring thing to do. Even if it is just to soak up the active lifestyle. Outdoor training in Sydney's Eastern suburbs has become very popular. At 6am our beaches are getting filled with lots of people who are doing bootcamp, personal training, walking, running, surfing, ... you name it!

Although Exercising on the soft sand is great, it is equally challenging. This means that you need to give yourself some time to get used it.

Not convinced yet?

Check out some of the benefits of beach training. 

Better for your joints

Landing on soft sand results in the fact that the overall stress and impact on your lower joints is a lot lower. On top of this, running on soft sand gives your calf muscles a great workout without the risk of any impact injuries. It can also reduce the risk of shin splints.

You'll burn up to 30% more calories

Training on the beach will definitely add some intensity to your training. Each strike or movement that you do, your feet sink in the sand. This forces you to exert more energy than you would on hard surface. Training on a beach can help you burn up 30% more calories. 

Prevent injuries

Running barefoot on sand makes smaller, stabilising muscles in the knees, ankles and feet work harder than running on the road with shoes. Training on the beach will strengthen these muscles and prevent common road injuries.

Go for a dip afterwards

Where there is a beach, there should be water. There is nothing more refreshing than jumping in the water after a great workout. Even if the water is a bit cool, it is still worth it and you'll feel amazing afterwards!

Enjoy the sceneries

We are very fortunate and should be very grateful to be able to train at Coogee and Bondi Beach. Training on the beach while watching the sunrise, has a lot more to offer than running on a treadmill while looking at a television screen.

Switch off

Although we live in a big and sometimes hectic city, spending time on a beach is a great way to reconnect with nature and to switch off.

title: Stir-fried vegetables and quinoa dish
seo_title: Vegetarian stir-fried vegetables and quinoa dish - Team One Fitness
seo_description: Try this amazing flavourful stir-fried vegetables and quina dish. It is a vegetarian meal but you can add chicken or salmon which works really well.
content:
Skip take-out and try this this flavourful stir-fried vegetables and quinoa dish

Ingredients

  • 1 cup uncooked quinoa (roughly 3 cups cooked quinoa)
  • 2 tbsp olive oil
  • 1 tbsp garlic, minced
  • 1 tbsp ginger, minced
  • 8 oz mushrooms, sliced
  • 12 oz broccoli florets, cut into small pieces
  • 2 medium carrots, sliced into think sticks
  • 1 cup peas
  • 2-3 eggs, beaten in a bowl
  • 4 tbsp reduced sodium soy sauce
  • 2 scallions, sliced for garnish
 

Preparation

  • In a medium pot, cook quinoa according to package instructions. Once cooked, fluff with a fork, then set aside.
  • In a large pan, heat oil, then sauté garlic and ginger until fragrant.
  • Add mushrooms, broccoli, and carrots. Stir until vegetables are tender.
  • Add cooked quinoa to the pan. Add peas and stir until well-mixed. Create a hole/space in the middle of the pan, add the eggs and mix egg to scramble. Once the egg is partially cooked, stir it in with the rest of the dish.
  • Add the soy sauce and give the dish a final stir.
  • Serve while hot. Garnish with sliced scallions (optional).
This is the vegetarian option.  I tried it last night adding chicken which worked well, but you could also use other meats or salmon. Click here for more yummy and healthy Team One Fitness recipes.

title: What are your New Years resolutions?
seo_description: The start of a new year is the best time to make some changes to our daily routine. Check out some tips to find your New Years Resolutions.
content:
The start of the new year seems is the best time to set goals and make some positive changes to our daily routine. The question is, what is the best way to come up with these resolutions?  What are your New Year resolutions? Below are a few tips: First of all new year resolutions can be about lots of different things, let's think about your health, social life, success at work, parenting skills, how to feel happier, etc.

Reflection

Ask yourself the following questions: What went well last year and what didn't? This will give you a better idea about where you would like to make some improvements.

Select 1 to 3 goals which will make a difference in your life

Think about what you would like to improve in your life and ask yourself how to do this. Choose a few goals and make sure they are specific.  This could be for example increasing your attendance at training, for example if you currently attend our Coogee Bootcamp or Bondi Bootcamp, you could give yourself a challenge to see if you can attend a lunchtime session at the Domain.  This is the perfect time of year to make the most of the outdoor training options the Eastern Suburbs has to offer. If you would like to lose five kilos, then this might involve making your portion sizes smaller, not eating carbs at night and exercising three to four times per week. Come up with a clear action plan which will help you to achieve your goals. Make your goals visible and write them down on a piece of paper. Let some family members and/or friends know about your resolutions as they can give you some support. Think about a plan B if certain things happen which may slow down the process of achieving your resolutions.

Have a 'stop-doing' list 

Feeling too busy often stops us from achieving our goals. To gain extra time to achieve your new resolutions, you will have to give up something else in your life. This might be staying up for one extra hour in the evening or checking your Facebook account five times a day. Basically, identify these things, put them on your 'stop-doing' list and don't do them.

title: AMRAP Five Plus

title: Get your butt off your chair
seo_title: Get your butt of your chair - Team One Fitness
seo_description: Research says to 'get your butt of your chair' more often. We need to focus on the exercise regime but also on the amount of time we spend being sedentary.
content:
A lot of research has been done about how much exercise we should do to live a healthy lifestyle. On the other hand research has shown that on top of this you should also get your butt of your chair more often. The message is, move more and sit less. These guidelines are officially known as 'Australia's Physical Activity and Sedentary Behaviour Guidelines', and they not only focus on the exercise part but also on the amount of time we spend being sedentary. In other words the time spent doing physical inactive tasks such as sitting or lying down. Experts say that we are sedentary on an average for about 7 to 10 hours a day which doesn't even include sleeping time. Studies have found that sedentary behaviour can be the cause of: obesity, heart disease, type 2 diabetes, some cancers, etc. In a nutshell, the goal is to try and reach the recommended time of daily exercising but on top of this to break your sedentary lifestyle by standing up, walking around regularly. Experts suggest you should aim not to sit down for longer then 20 to 30 minutes.

So how can we do this? Here are a few ideas.

At work:

  • Try and encourage standing or walking meetings or if this doesn't work you could have a standing break.
  • Join one of our lunchtime CBD Domain bootcamp sessions or go for a walk/run in the park.
  • Stand up when you are on the phone or reading emails.
  • Set up your office material such as printers, rubbish bins, drawers away from your desk so you need to get out of your chair.
  • Try and walk to your colleagues to talk to them instead of sending an email.
  • Put little reminders to get of your chair more often.
  • Drink more water which will make you go the toilet more often.
 

At home

  • Stand up or walk when on the phone.
  • Stand up when you're watching TV and doing domestic chores such as ironing or folding washing.
  • Embrace domestic chores.
  • Work in the garden.
  • Wash your car yourself instead of taking it to the carwash.
  • Walk or ride a bike instead of using the car.

The Workout

See below for the workout as I did it, but feel free to make changes according your fitness level. Aim to perform 30 reps per set but adjust this number according to your level of fitness (e.g. 20/25/30) and the weight you use for the workout. Try and use a weight which allows you to perform a high number of reps (male: 12-24kg ; female: 6-16kg). Perform 3 rounds for time of the following exercises below.
  • 30x skipping double-unders or normal skipping (triple the reps, e.g. 90 reps)
  • 30x 20kg barbell shoulder push presses
  • 30x 12kg lateral wall balls
  • 30x 20kg barbell walking lunges
  • 30x push ups
  • 500m run

No equipment available?

If you have no equipment available, you could modify the workout and do 3 rounds for time of the following exercises :
  • 30x tuck jumps
  • 30x mountain climbers r/l
  • 30 Russian twist r/l
  • 30x walking lunges or jumping lunges
  • 30x push ups
  • 500m run
  Give it a crack, I think you'll enjoy it! Can't make it to one of our Eastern Suburbs group training sessions? Check out some other workouts which you could do in your own time.

title: Simple swaps for a better & healthier life
seo_title: Simple changes for a better & healthier life - Team One Fitness
seo_description: We all want the highest possible quality of life. Here are a bunch of simple changes for a better & healthier life.
content:
Whole grains for white, quality for quantity, standing for sitting at a desk or throwing a frisbee on Bondi Beach for sunbathing. Some little changes can help you to live a happier and healthier life. Check out a few 'this for that's' which can increase your quality of life.

Gym for napping

Tired after work or during the day?  Squeeze in quick workout which will boost your enery levels, and burn some calories.  

Foam rolling for static stretching

Feeling sore and need to get rid of some knots in your muscles? Use a foam roller rather than stretching. Time for both? Great, use the foam roller first and then stretch the muscles you've been working on.  

Stairs for escalator

Probably not the first time that you've heard this tip but here he goes again... take the escalator instead of the stairs, and burn some calories!  

Active date for dinner date

Do something different on your date and instead of going for a meal, do the Bondi to Coogee coastal walk, go wall climbing, ice skating or go for a hike.  

Interval workout for relaxed run

Nothing wrong with long distance jogging and I strongly believe there is a place for every type of training. If you do like long distance jogging, maybe try a 20-minute high intensity interval workout that involves some sprints and other strength and cardio exercises. It may spice things up a bit and give you overall better and faster results.  

Cooking home for eating out

Although it's nice to go out for a meal and this is totally fine, cooking at home will more likely result in a healthier meal.  

Whole fruit for fruit juice

Compare having a whole orange with a glass of fresh orange juice. An orange will give you the pulp, skin, and full fiber content. Don't choose the juice option or you'll miss out on all the extra benefits.
 

Biking to work for public transport

Is your office not too far away? Take the bike or walk instead of taking the bus or train. Even better, wake up a little earlier and do one of our Bondi or Coogee bootcamp classes! Doing some kind of exercise will boost your endorphins and can make your day more productive.  

Red wine or beer for Margaritas

Choose a red wine or vodka and soda, rather than a sugary cocktail and consume about half of the calories. Want to know more about the best and worst alcohol drinks for weight loss? check out the link.   

Outside for inside

Most of us spend plenty of time indoors. Use your free time to get some fresh air and hopefully soak up some sun. Fresh air and vitamin D makes you feel happier and gives you more energy. Do you have an office job, don't get to spend a lot of time outside but want to keep fit? Do some outdoor training rather than spending more time indoors in a gym.  

Little goals for long term goals

Long term goals are important but don't forget about the little goals and milestones which will help you to reach those big goals. Don't forget the small achievements that you make which will add up to positive change!

title: Never miss a Monday training session
seo_title: Never miss a Monday training session
seo_description: Waking up for a 6am Monday training session ain't easy, especially in winter! Check out some reasons why you should never miss a Monday training session.
content:
Being woken from your slumber at 5.15am on a Monday morning when it's still dark and chilly, is not always the most welcoming start of the week. Pressing snooze a few times can be very tempting and deciding to stay in bed, even more tempting! Well, here are a few reasons why it is good to get your butt of bed and Never miss a Monday training session.  

You'll feel better and happier

Every single Monday I see people rocking up to our Bondi or Coogee morning session with a 'tired, I would rather be in bed' face. This is even more so in the winter months. 45 minutes later, every single one of them, walks off with a smile on their face (including me)! As research shows, exercising releases endorphins and will make you feel better. There is nothing better (well nearly nothing) than the positive vibes that flow though your brain and body after doing a great session. Studies say that the average office worker only cracks their first smile at 11.15am. Why not crack it at 6am? You'll be 5 hours and 15 minutes ahead of the average Joe!  

More likely to work out for the rest of the week

Training on a Monday often sets the workout regime for the rest of the week. It gets the ball rolling and sets you up for feeling motivated for the following four/five days of exercise.  

Reduce anxious thoughts

Do you sometimes feel anxious, particularly on a Monday morning? This is not uncommon as many people struggle with this Monday morning phenomenon. Thinking about the work load which is waiting for you can make you feel anxious. Studies have shown that exercising and mainly aerobic exercises will reduce your anxiety levels. Also interesting to note is that high intensity training will reduce your anxiety sensitivity or in  other words the fear of anxiety which often comes before panic attacks.  

Sleep Better

Research shows that resistance training can reboot your body clock. One study showed that 4 months of consistent training helped chronic insomniacs sleep 45min more per night.

title: Things not to eat
seo_description: Maintaining a healthy diet ain't always easy and is often easier said than done. Here is a list of a few things which you better not include in your diet.
content:
Maintaining a healthy diet ain't always easy and is often easier said than done. Here is a list of a few things not to eat. Avoid them and replace them with healthier options.

 

Fast Breakfast

Your body is an engine and feeding it with breakfast fuel from fast food joints is a mistake. Fat, sugar, salt and chemicals doesn't make it ready for an active day. The same counts for morning breakfast drinks. Maybe they contain protein but think about the chemicals, sugar and other unhealthy sugar substitutes. Take an extra 10 minutes each morning to cook up some wholesome food.  

Food in Tins

Food courts often serve hot food tins loaded with MSG. MSG (monosodium glutamate) is a food additive used as a flavour enhancer. It basically makes cheap quality meat taste better. One of the side effects of MSG is that it leads to weight gain, liver and brain damage.  Apparently restaurants and cafes have no legal requirements to declare the presence of MSG in food so it's pretty hard to find out what you're eating. MSG is an excitotoxin in the brain, meaning that it overstimulates the brain causing the production of excessive amounts of dopamine. This creates a drum-like rush that provides a brief sensation of wellbeing. It's highly addictive, causing its consumers to keep coming back for more and end up overeating, meanwhile destroying brain cells.  

Late Night Crap

It is spring and we're probably all having a few more drinks than normal. Enjoy your drinks in moderation but don't finish the night with large fizzy drinks combined with fast food like burgers, kebabs etc. Also stay away from consuming other high in sugar snacks. If you have been drinking a little too much, tough it out and deal with it in a healthy way.

title: Summer bodies are built in winter
seo_description: Do you want to feel and look fit in summer then don't waste any winter. Check out why and how summer bodies are built in winter.
content:
Lack of energy and lack of motivation are very common in winter. This article is all about being aware that summer bodies are built in winter and how to get you out of the ‘winter blues’. Temperatures have dropped and as temperatures drop, often our motivation to keep fit drops as well. Although spring seems like a long time away, it will be around the corner before you know it! Time flies and so do these few months of colder weather.

A big step ahead

People who keep their fitness levels up during winter are a big step ahead of the people who go into hibernation mode. It is very easy to go into hibernation mode and I know that staying in bed on a dark and cold morning can be very tempting! Being inactive will definitely affect your cardio and fitness levels. It’s good to know though that in general, your strength and cardio levels decrease slower than most people think. Although cardio levels decrease quicker than strength, it is easier to build back up again. Less exercising and hibernation mode often go hand in hand with an unhealthier diet. Keep in mind that being inactive and bad nutrition can result in fast weight gain. If you can keep your fitness routine up during these tough winter months, you’ll be a big step ahead of all those people who didn’t.

How to keep it up

There are a lot of things that you can do that will help you to get through these winter months as healthy and actively as possible.

Goals

Set your training goals, both short and long term. For example what do you intend to achieve this week in terms of training sessions? And what would you like to achieve by the end of winter?

Routine

Routine is key! Once you know your goals, put a workout plan together. Make sure the plan is sufficient so it will make you reach your goals. Make sure that your plan is achievable.

Tips for waking up

If you’re an early morning exerciser then you will probably know that getting out of bed is the hardest bit. Check out here some tips which help you to make waking up easier.

The right gear

If you like outdoor training and you want to keep this up in winter, make sure that you have the right gear to exercise. The right clothing will make you feel comfortable and will make a big difference. Check out some tips about which winter workout gear to use.

Make it work

Make changes to your routine to make it work. If you’re not managing to get out of bed in the morning to exercise, change your routine and pick another time which will work better for you. If you’re not managing the cold and can’t get yourself into outdoor training, change your routine and keep active by doing something else for a little while. You can make every change, and you should, making sure that you’re on your way to reaching your goals.

Nutrition

Stay on top of your diet. If you feel that you’re exercising less than usual, make sure that you change your nutritional intake. Keep your nutritional expenditure and intake in balance.   You’ve probably heard the following things a zillion times but it is good to keep reminding yourself that:
  • You’ll feel so much better after completing a workout. Exercising is great for keeping your head clear and will improve your quality of life in every aspect.
  • Once you start working out, you’ll be warm in no time.
  • There is nothing better than starting the day with some fresh air, watching the sun come up and maybe even spotting a whale.
  • You don’t want to start all over again once spring starts. You’ll be a massive step ahead of the big horde who didn’t stay fit during winter!

title: The best and worst alcohol drinks for weight loss
seo_title: The best and worst alcohol drinks for weight loss
seo_description: Are you on a weight loss journey but you do like a drink sometimes, then check out this list of the best and worst alcohol drinks for weight loss.
content:
Are you on a weight loss journey and don't want to undo your results from your weight loss efforts? Check out the list of the best and worst alcohol drinks for weight loss.

THE BEST

Wine 

A glass of red or white whine contains about 100 to 120 calories per glass. In general white wine has less carbohydrates than red wine which makes a small difference when it comes down to calories. Interesting to note is that red wine on the other hand is richer in antioxidants, and its ellargic acids delay the growth of fat cells with the result of slowing the development of new ones.

Vermouth

Vermouth is mainly popular in France and Italy. It is a wine flavoured with spices and herbs. It's alcohol content is quite high (15 to 18 %) and one glass only has about 64 calories. Vermouth is full of polyphenol compounds which may promote healthy weight loss. Just make sure that you don't mix it in a Martini as this will bump up your calorie and sugar intake.

Liquors

If you want the highest alcohol content and the lowest amount of calories, shots and straight booze on the rocks are the way to go. All of the main liquors have a similar amount of calories and carbohydrates but in general they say, the stronger the liquor, the higher the calories. A shot of whisky has about 105 calories, while vodka 97. Don't mix it up with sweet drinks if you want to keep the calories down (Vodka Red Bull, Rum Coke, etc) and go for the plain option. Instead, add some squeezed lemon or lime if you want to give it some more taste.

Light Beers

Light beers are lower in calories and carbs which makes them the beers to go for if you're keeping an eye on your weight. They are lower in alcohol so don't fall in the trap of drinking too many. This might give you the opposite effect.

THE WORST

Sugary Cocktails

Long island Iced Teas and Margaritas can have more calories than a big order of chips. They are for a lot of people the good stuff but unfortunately won't help you to shed some weight. The thing with these cocktails is that our bodies don't properly metabolise the sugar. Instead our bodies will store the sweet stuff as fat.

High Alcohol Special beer

Sorry to all my Belgian friends but all the good special Belgium beers are high in calories. Duvel, La Chouffe, Chimay, you name it, they all have more calories than you would think. A 330ml of Duvel has 198 calories while a Chimay on the other hand has 212 calories. The rule is, the higher the alcohol content, the more calories. The good thing is that you wouldn't be able to drink these beers at the same pace as a normal standard beer, ... unless you've been practising a lot :) Oh, and one more thing, getting on the booze often goes hand in hand with feeling hungry (or at least you think you feel hungry). Watch what you eat after a few drinks and don't let yourself get dragged into McDonalds :). Your body probably doesn't need it and can do without it!
